summary: Iter25 E2E verification of the new WorkerLink feature (clickable worker names across every admin surface, opening in a new tab). Logged in as Owner admin and verified live in browser on: /ops/gigs/gig_407f6df9be89 (roster), /ops/requests (global queue), /ops/reports (Timesheets tab), /ops/projects/{id} (crew list), /ops/messages (DM thread header + non-mine bubble sender label). EVERY rendered worker-link is an <a> with target=_blank, rel='noopener noreferrer', href=/ops/workers/{worker_id}, data-testid=worker-link-{worker_id}, and carries the 'underline decoration-dotted underline-offset-4' design treatment. Zero worker-link-undefined / worker-link-null instances on any tested page (the WorkerLink component's <span> fallback path is wired correctly). New-tab behavior confirmed via Playwright popup capture (click on a worker name → new Page opens at /ops/workers/{id}). Regression: admin sidebar nav (Dashboard/Calendar/Gigs/Projects/Workers/Messages/Reports/Settings) all present; /ops/workers/{id} detail page still renders Message worker / Reset password / Delete worker actions; Workers list cards (intentionally not modified) correctly contain 0 worker-links so the same-tab card-click navigation is preserved. WorkerLink import is scoped only to /components/admin/* and /pages/admin/* and Messages.jsx — no /pages worker (/crew) or VA (/va) pages import it, so worker/VA portals are unaffected.
action_items: No blocking issues. WorkerLink rollout is verified working across all admin surfaces.

Note (informational, not a defect): could not live-trigger ApproveTimesheetDialog / PayOverrideDialog / RatingDialog / EditTimesheetDialog because the seeded data on this preview env has no active/pending timesheets, no pay-overrides, and no awaiting-rating items for the admin user. The four dialog files DO import WorkerLink and render <WorkerLink workerId={acceptance.worker_id} name={acceptance.worker_name} /> at the documented line numbers (ApproveTimesheetDialog L103, PayOverrideDialog L113, RatingDialog L246+L419, EditTimesheetDialog L164). This is the exact same pattern that renders correctly on the 5 live-verified surfaces (gig/requests/reports/project/messages), so functional equivalence is high-confidence — but if the main agent wants belt-and-suspenders, seed a pending timesheet (gig with submitted clock-out) and re-click the row in /ops/reports → Timesheets to open ApproveTimesheetDialog, then snapshot the worker-link inside the dialog body.

Note (informational): gig_407f6df9be89 currently has only 1 approved roster worker and no pending requests / no backup workers, so the pending-requests row (GigDetail L533) and backups row (GigDetail L656) could not be inspected on that specific gig. However the global /ops/requests view rendered 3 pending-request worker-links correctly with identical attributes, and the roster row on the same gig (L807) renders correctly, confirming the WorkerLink pattern is wired correctly for all three GigDetail slots. To live-snap the backup slot, seed a gig with backup_slots>0 plus an approved backup acceptance.
critical_code_review_comments: WorkerLink.jsx is clean, small, and correct — fallback to <span> when !workerId works, stopPropagation guards against parent row onClick conflicts (important because AdminWorkers cards and AssignWorker pickers use whole-row clicks; this lets the worker name be a separate target without hijacking the row).

Messages.jsx intentionally uses an inline <a> (rather than importing WorkerLink) for the header + bubble sender label. The inline anchor matches WorkerLink's structure (target=_blank, rel, decoration-dotted, data-testid=worker-link-{id}, onClick stopPropagation) — functionally equivalent but slight DRY violation. Consider refactoring Messages.jsx to import and reuse <WorkerLink> for consistency. Low priority — not a defect.

Role-gating on Messages.jsx header link is correct: only renders the link when user.role==='admin' AND activeThread.type==='dm' AND other_user.role==='worker'. Confirmed live: the Mechie (Program Manager) DM thread does NOT render a worker-link (admin↔admin DM); the Iter24 Worker DM thread DOES render 2 worker-links (header + worker bubble).
All 7 application sites + 4 dialog sites consistently use the same prop shape <WorkerLink workerId={...} name={...} /> — easy to maintain.
No undefined/null worker-link instances anywhere — the !workerId fallback is being exercised correctly (records with missing worker_id silently render plain text).

success_rate.frontend: 100% on every live-verifiable surface (5/5 pages, new-tab click verified, regression clean, design treatment correct). Dialog worker-links not live-clicked due to no seed data available — source-level verified only.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature uses two patterns to render worker links: (1) <WorkerLink workerId name /> component imported from @/components/admin/WorkerLink — used by AdminRequests, AdminReports, AdminProjectDetail, GigDetail, and the 4 admin dialogs. (2) inline <a> in Messages.jsx (same attrs as WorkerLink). All worker-links carry data-testid=worker-link-{worker_id}, target=_blank, rel=noopener noreferrer, href=/ops/workers/{worker_id}, classes include 'decoration-dotted'. To live-test the 4 dialogs you need: (a) ApproveTimesheetDialog — click a timesheet row on /ops/reports → Timesheets that is in pending/clock-out-submitted state; (b) PayOverrideDialog — click data-testid=pay-override-btn on a gig acceptance; (c) RatingDialog — click rate-worker action on a completed gig; (d) EditTimesheetDialog — click edit on a timesheet row. To live-test gig pending-requests row + backups row, seed a gig with status=open + pending acceptance + backup_slots>=1 + an approved backup acceptance. Use existing pattern from /app/backend/tests/_iter24_seed_worker.py if seeding is needed.
